chunks: From him, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:

He was asked about a man who missed one rak'ah of the Maghrib prayer with the Imam and caught the two [remaining] rak'ahs; so the first is for him and the second is for the people, and he sits for the tashahhud in it. He [the Imam] said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And the second [rak'ah] as well?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'All of them?' He said, 'Yes, for it is only a blessing.'
ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs does a person count if they join congregational prayer late and miss only one rak'ah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific fiqh of joining congregational prayer late, establishing that the missed rak'ah is counted as personal qada while subsequent ones follow the Imam, with the worshipper performing tashahhud in each. The Imam’s confirmation that 'it is merely a blessing' (innama huwa barakah) highlights the Shia scholarly view that the extra sitting is not a redundant burden but a spiritual merit, reflecting the generosity of divine law. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining congregational unity even when joining late, as the additional acts are viewed as compensatory grace rather than strict obligation.
